newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Wednesday.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed today amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bills yields were slightly higher but bond prices were steady to slightly lower. The interbank rate was unchanged and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.45/2.40 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 2.41/2.36 percent.
One-year treasury bills closed at a yield of 2.18/2.13 percent against 2.12/2.07 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 was unchanged from Tuesday's close of S$98.15/98.20.
September 2001 ended at S$97.53/97.58 versus Tuesday's close of S$97.70/97.75 and June 2003 at S$96.35/96.40 against S$96.63/96.68.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from Tuesday's 3-5/16 3-3/16 percent.
